prompt_text: I need braces or Invisalign in Denver. Which specific orthodontists should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best orthodontist in Denver for braces or Invisalign?
answer_verbatim:
I can absolutely help — I just need one quick detail to make the recommendations useful: what neighborhood or ZIP code in Denver are you in (or willing to travel to)? Also tell me whether this is for an adult or a child, and what matters most to you (cost, speed, discreetness, weekend hours, an orthodontist who does complex cases, accepts your insurance, etc.). With that I’ll give 3–6 specific local orthodontists to call and exactly why each is a good match.

While you reply, here’s a quick plan and a set of things to ask when you call so you get comparable answers:

How I pick the practices I’ll recommend
- Board-certified orthodontists / AAO members (orthodontists—not general dentists)  
- Good recent patient reviews and before/after photos for Invisalign/braces  
- Experience with adult cases (if relevant) and clear payment/insurance options  
- Use of modern tech (digital scans like iTero, 3D imaging) which makes Invisalign planning and braces more accurate  
- Convenient location/hours if you say proximity matters

What to ask each office when you call (script-style)
- “Are you an orthodontist who specializes in braces and Invisalign, or is this an orthodontist supervised by a general dentist?” (Ask for the doctor’s name and credentials.)
- “Is Dr. X board certified by the American Board of Orthodontics (if applicable) and a member of the American Association of Orthodontists (AAO)?”
- “Does Dr. X treat adults/teens/children? How many Invisalign cases do you do per year?” (High volume often means more experience with aligners.)
- “Do you use a digital intraoral scanner (iTero or similar) for aligner impressions?”  
- “Roughly how long would treatment take for someone with crowding/overbite/... (briefly describe your concern)?”  
- “What is a typical price range for Invisalign vs braces, and what financing/insurance options do you offer?”  
- “Do you offer a free or low-cost consultation and are there before/after photos or patient testimonials I can see?”  
- “What is your policy for emergencies or broken brackets/attachments?”  

Red flags to avoid
- Offices that push a single product (e.g., only their own-brand aligner) without explaining alternatives  
- No doctor listed (or the treatment supervised by a general dentist)  
- No digital records or before/after photos to review  
- Vague cost answers without a consultation/scan

If you tell me your ZIP code and priorities I’ll send 3–6 specific Denver-area orthodontists (names, phone numbers, a short reason to call each) and a recommended first choice based on your needs.
